subject: Hyperscaler comparison & private control-plane feasibility — recap and next actions
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bates <simon.bates@grayrock.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:22:00 +0100
Subject: Hyperscaler comparison & private control-plane feasibility — recap and next actions

Hi Simon — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a shared checklist and can run the right tests next week.

Call summary (high level):
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for GrayRock inference (sensitive financial models).
- Main risks you flagged vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints: control-plane egress, KMS/HSM integration, auditability of requests, and the ability to run fully air-gapped inference for a small set of workloads.
- Performance target: 95thpct tail < 120ms for 512-token chat sessions; baseline throughput roughly 100 concurrent users.

Items we agreed to own / next steps from Redwood:
1) Short brief comparing control-plane architectures (Redwood private vs major hyperscalers) — attached (redwood-controlplane-brief.pdf).
2) Confirm which control-plane traffic must remain inside your VPC vs what can be egressed through a managed control endpoint. We suggested two modes: "control plane in-VPC" (private API endpoint + customer-managed control plane) and "control plane peered" (minimal telemetry egress to Redwood metrics endpoints).
3) Run a lightweight smoke test from your staging VPC to measure outbound control-plane connectivity and measured latency to a pinned model variant. (Marcus / Ben to coordinate infra test steps.)
4) KMS/HSM options & audit logs: we listed our KMS integrations and proposed an audit-retention SLA. We'll produce concrete HSM/KMS integration checklist.

Attachments: redwood-controlplane-brief.pdf (pdf, ~450KB) — short comparative notes + network diagrams.

Estimated timeline: smoke test + initial latency numbers by Sept 1; KMS/HSM checklist by Sept 3.

Could you confirm: 1) Which internal subnets we should target for the smoke test, and 2) whether you need an NDA or additional legal controls before we share more low-level PII/telemetry examples?

Thanks — I’ll loop engineering once you confirm the subnet.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com | +44 7700 555 101

--

redwood.com

From: Simon Bates <simon.bates@grayrock.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Hyperscaler comparison & private control-plane feasibility — recap and next actions

Thanks Olga — appreciate the write-up. A few clarifications from our side:

- Subnets for smoke test: use staging-subnet-3 (10.12.34.0/24) behind our transit gateway — that's the one with the firewall rules closest to prod.
- Air-gap: for one classification model (regulatory screening) we need an option to run truly air-gapped for up to 30 days (no outbound connectivity at runtime). We understand that implies a different control-plane model — please outline constraints for that in the KMS/HSM checklist.
- KMS: we use a cloud HSM (Thales) via KMIP. It must support key wrapping; if you need a short-term bridge please state the proposed rotation & audit steps.
- Audit logs: 7 years retention for a subset of audit events (access to model X) is a hard requirement.

For the smoke test, we can share a simple network sketch (attached) and will create a temporary IAM principal that you can use to connect. We do want a short technical deep-dive (30m) with your infra/eng team before tests start to confirm traffic flows.

Attachment: grayrock-network-sketch.png (png)

Simon
Simon Bates
Head of Platform Security | GrayRock AI
simon.bates@grayrock.ai

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:07:00 +0100

Yes — I can run the smoke test. Quick plan:
- Prep: use the staging IAM principal Simon will provide and test from a small EC2 instance inside staging-subnet-3.
- Tests to capture: TLS handshake, token exchange latency, initial model load time, a 1-minute sustained 10 qps run to check tail latency.
- Deliverable: short runbook + CSV with p50/p95/p99 numbers and packet capture snippets if we see retransmits.

I attached a draft runbook we can use (smoke-test-runbook.md). I also propose we record the session and upload results to the shared Drive folder.

I’ll start setup tomorrow and aim to run tests Aug 31 (UTC hours). If infra needs to be pulled in, ping me and I’ll loop them.

Ben
